args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error after us-east, leaving the regions on mixed versions); a retry finished the rollout. All regions are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and the rollback orchestrator error.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001). The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production, and its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging. No approval was needed, since v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Rollback:** The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving regions on different versions. I retried once and that finished the job. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0 now, and the error rate has dropped from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first request to create it timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key (a tag that stops a retry from creating a second incident). Only one incident exists, and on-call has been paged. It covers what failed, the rollback, the partial failure and retry, and the current status.

Two things still need follow-up: why v2.3.1 failed, and what caused the orchestrator error during the rollback.
